subject: The Attention Brief #05 — This week’s reading list and evidence check
headline: This week’s reading list and evidence check
deck: Coverage update: this week’s research synthesis is still under review. The available source shelf is below; no new findings or cross-paper conclusions are being endorsed in this update.
letter: This week’s eligible reading shelf contains 2 source-backed records. These are records with substantive source material and a verified publication date in the covered week. Availability does not establish the quality of an individual study or mean that a summary has passed review. A complete synthesis is not ready. This dated update keeps the weekly archive current and makes the coverage gap visible. A checked analysis can replace this update at the same permanent link.

signals.title: Read the available originals
signals.text: The source shelf links to the available originals and identifies the material available for each record. Treat an abstract as a limited account and distinguish a research report from commentary. The shelf is a starting point for reading; it is not a claim that every relevant publication was found.

tension.title: What remains open
tension.text: The evidence synthesis remains pending. Until it is checked, this update makes no claim about whether AI helps or harms attention, learning, or wellbeing. When reading the linked material, ask what was measured, whose experience was represented, and whether a conclusion concerns association, interpretation, or a tested intervention.

closer: Which claims can the available designs support, and which questions still need better evidence?

experiment.title: Keep a reading question
experiment.text: Choose one source and write down a question its design can answer and a question it leaves open.
experiment.caution: A reading prompt, not a tested attention intervention.
